tweets.text:
Can the same computation secure a blockchain and power AI models?

Pearl is a Proof-of-Useful-Work blockchain designed to let miners perform AI inference and compete for blocks using the same computation. The goal is to create two complementary revenue streams: block rewards help subsidize inference, while customer payments help cover the underlying cost of mining.

Pearl uses matrix multiplication as its mining primitive, which is also a core operation in AI inference. When a miner processes a compatible inference request, the same calculations can generate mining attempts while producing an output that serves a customer.

But miners can also perform arbitrary matrix multiplications solely to compete for block rewards. The protocol verifies that the prescribed computation was performed correctly, not whether the matrices originated from a real inference request.

The economic incentive is straightforward. Miners performing real inference can earn customer fees and mining rewards from the same underlying work, potentially improving their economics relative to miners performing synthetic calculations alone.

The remaining challenge is converting that incentive into realized utility: how much of the network's total computation is actually serving external demand rather than being performed solely to earn block rewards?

On March 12, 2023, New York regulators seized Signature Bank, just days after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank and Silvergate’s decision to liquidate. 

Regulators claimed that Signature faced a crisis of confidence and dangerous deposit outflows. 

Unfortunately, they were not being truthful. As @nic_carter has written extensively about — the government was actually just using the banking system to cut the crypto industry off from the dollar. This is what became known as “Operation Choke Point 2.0.”

The years since have added important context. FDIC documents released in 2025 showed banks seeking to engage with crypto were repeatedly met with delays, demands for more information, and requests to pause activity. 

In 2023 Signature was one of the most important banks serving the industry, making what happened that weekend a pivotal moment in the story. 

Last month I sat down with Signature Bank’s founder to hear, in his own words, what happened inside the bank as regulators moved in — and why he believes Signature never needed to be seized.

This is one of the most important and interesting interviews I’ve done to date. I hope you all enjoy.

On March 12, 2023, New York regulators seized Signature Bank, just days after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank and Silvergate’s decision to liquidate. 

Regulators claimed that Signature faced a crisis of confidence and dangerous deposit outflows. 

Unfortunately, they were not being truthful. As @nic_carter has written extensively about — the government was actually just using the banking system to cut the crypto industry off from the dollar. This is what became known as “Operation Choke Point 2.0.”

The years since have added important context. FDIC documents released in 2025 showed banks seeking to engage with crypto were repeatedly met with delays, demands for more information, and requests to pause activity. 

In 2023 Signature was one of the most important banks serving the industry, making what happened that weekend a pivotal moment in the story. 

Last month I sat down with Signature Bank’s founder to hear, in his own words, what happened inside the bank as regulators moved in — and why he believes Signature never needed to be seized.

This is one of the most important and interesting interviews I’ve done to date. I hope you all enjoy.

inefficiency = free money.

here’s how you can combine Jev and Claude to rank every upcoming catalyst on your watchlist:

1: Get a Jev API key
2: Save the key in a .env file in your project
3: Install TypeSafe's official skill in Claude Code so it knows how to call Jev correctly.
4: Ask Claude Code to set up a project (Python with a TypeSafe key, or TypeScript with a Vercel Gateway key) with separate files for your token watchlist, your Jev questions and your score thresholds.
5: Add a CLAUDE. md file saying that Jev only scores text, code handles all numbers and dates.
6: Have Claude Code build fetchers that collect governance proposals, project announcements, releases and unlock schedules for every token on your watchlist.
7: Convert every item into the same simple record: project, title, text, source link and event date.
8: Calculate how many days away each event is in code, because Jev cannot reliably compare dates.
9: Send each item to Jev in a single call that asks all your questions at once, which keeps it fast and cheap.
10: Ask Jev what type of catalyst it is, how much it could matter, how specific the timing is, and whether it is a recap or just hype.
11: Combine Jev's answers in code into one priority score, using weights you set and can change.
12: Route every item: drop non-catalysts, put unclear ones on a review list, and flag high-priority items and serious security incidents for a brief.
13: Have Claude read the full source for each flagged item and write a short brief.
14: Run it next to your normal research for a week and compare its picks with yours before you trust it.
15: Fix the questions or weights wherever it got things wrong, then test again.
16: Save the workflow as a Claude Skill and set up a scheduled task to run it once or twice a day.

start turning your knowledge into alpha asap.
